intuition.title: Proposed phase transfer, reduction and recovery
intuition.text: The authors describe a liquid ethanol/linoleic-acid phase, solid sodium linoleate and a water/ethanol phase containing Ag ions. They propose Ag-ion exchange into silver linoleate, reduction by ethanol at interfaces, outward-facing alkyl chains and gravity-assisted phase separation. These are the paper’s mechanism interpretation; silver linoleate, ligand coverage and phase compositions were not directly measured.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 2, hydrothermal preparation and mechanism

intuition.title: Particle cores and assembled monolayers are distinct
intuition.text: The TEM specimen shows round, smooth Ag particles, a reported diameter of 5.0 ± 0.3 nm and ordered arrays on a carbon-film/Cu support. The ± statistic is unspecified. The authors interpret the smooth packing as diffusion outpacing arrival during grid drying; it does not establish a measured diffusion coefficient or a separate synthesis.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF pp. 2–3, TEM method, Figure 1 and packing discussion

intuition.title: Surface identity remains unresolved
intuition.text: The preparation and Figure 2 discussion describe linoleic-acid passivation, while Figure 1 and the interlinking discussion refer to sodium linoleate tails. Both descriptions are kept as source-proposed context; neither is a measured bound-ligand structure or a resolved identity assignment.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF pp. 2–3, Figure 1 caption, passivation and Figure 2 discussion

intuition.title: Spacing and weak plasmon absorption
intuition.text: The source reports a center-separation/particle-diameter ratio D/2r of approximately 1.75. It associates weak plasmon absorption with small particle cores and ordered separation. No absolute interparticle gap, shell thickness, quantitative coupling constant or absorption-peak wavelength is inferred.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF pp. 3–4, Figure 3 and D/2r discussion

intuition.title: PL explanation is a hypothesis
intuition.text: The measured 390 nm PL band is obtained with 250 nm excitation on quartz. The authors propose radiative sp-electron/d-hole recombination enhanced by a combination of surface plasmon and an electrostatic mechanism analogous to SERS. This source does not supply its own Raman measurement, absolute PL quantum yield or time-resolved mechanism test.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF pp. 3–4, optical methods and mechanism

intuition.title: Cited variations do not become new recipes
intuition.text: Temperature control of core size, alternative fatty-acid/sodium-stearate combinations and electronic transitions appear as cited discussion, including an unpublished reference. No separate source-defined charge, temperature series or measured conductivity outcome is supplied here.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 3, cited size and ligand variations; p. 4, reference 12

general_background.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
general_background.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
